claims.text: OpenAI News RSS timestamped the Agents API public-beta release at 2026-09-10T00:00:00Z.
claims.sourceLocator: RSS item pubDate

claims.text: OpenAI says the Agents API is available in public beta to all developers with no additional API fee, while models, tools and hosted sandbox compute retain their applicable charges.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 Start building; s3 Pricing; s4 Pricing

claims.text: The Agents API manages sessions, orchestration, context compaction and recovery while the application provides tools and chooses the execution environment.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 opening overview and core concepts

claims.text: The application remains responsible for deciding which data, tools and actions are available and for checking external state to determine whether work actually succeeded.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: application-provided tools and environment; application-handled required actions; sandbox code access; separate external systems. Boundary: operational design inference, not an OpenAI guarantee.

claims.text: Cancelling an active turn is distinct from deleting a session, and closing a hosted-sandbox event stream does not cancel the task.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 Sandbox expiry; s7 Delete a session note

claims.text: OpenAI-hosted sandboxes enable outbound network access by default unless a template supplies another policy, and support disabled or exact-host restricted modes.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 Control network access table

claims.text: In a self-hosted setup, OpenAI runs the harness while an executor in the builder's environment receives commands over an outbound connection using a restricted environment key.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 How the connection works; Authentication

claims.text: Agents API session state currently supports only United States data residency and does not support Zero Data Retention, including with a self-hosted sandbox.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 data-controls note lines 1401-1402

claims.text: Agent-generated code can access the files, credentials and network exposed to its environment; OpenAI recommends isolated workloads, separated keys and brokered third-party access.
claims.sourceLocator: s6 lines 861-887

claims.text: Detailed trace retrieval and external trace exporters are not part of the public-beta customer API, and usage values are best-effort rather than a final bill.

The WildClawBench preprint reports 60 human-authored tasks averaging more than 20 tool calls, a best overall result of 62.2 per cent across 19 models, and up to an 18-point change for one model when the harness changed.
claims.sourceLocator: s9 abstract

claims.text: Mittal's preprint reports analysis of 10,664 trajectories across nine models and four task families, with the agentic task falling from near-perfect success to near zero within 16 dependent steps.
claims.sourceLocator: s10 abstract

claims.text: METR defines time horizon by the human-expert duration of a task at a given predicted success probability, not by agent connection time, and warns that current measurements above 16 hours are unreliable.
claims.sourceLocator: s11 definition, measurement warning and FAQ

claims.text: A managed harness may reduce orchestration work, but the adoption decision should be based on repeated end-to-end outcomes, failure recovery, authority, cancellation, data fit and total accepted-result cost.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: managed capabilities and constraints plus independent evidence that harness and horizon affect outcomes. Boundary: proposed evaluation framework, not measured Agents API performance.

claims.text: A session can receive input, stream or expose progress through webhooks, stop for required application action, continue or be steered, delegate to subagents and resume where it left off; skills, MCP, web search and programmatic tool calling are configurable capabilities.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 A session from start to finish and What the managed harness provides; s7 Handle required actions. Final copy uses the supported wording 'resume a session where it left off'.

claims.text: Standardising session state, compaction, reconnection and delegated-work mechanics can reduce an application's orchestration burden, but the benefit depends on the existing implementation.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s2 and s3 describe the managed harness and session lifecycle; s5 documents executor reconnection. Boundary: Index Us engineering inference, not measured effort reduction.

claims.text: OpenAI describes three compute routes for the Agents API: an OpenAI-managed sandbox, the builder's own infrastructure and supported sandbox partners.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 Choose your agent environment. Final copy acknowledges all three routes and explicitly limits the detailed comparison to OpenAI-hosted and self-hosted options.

claims.text: Beginning a pilot with a minimal environment, narrow network access, separate workloads and brokered or revocable credentials is a risk-reduction recommendation rather than a tested Agents API result.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s4 network modes and configurable files/packages; s5 restricted executor key; s6 isolation, approved endpoints and credential brokering. Boundary: Index Us deployment recommendation.

claims.text: The current United States-only session-state residency and lack of ZDR can make the API unsuitable for some regulated, contractual or highly sensitive workloads.
claims.sourceLocator: Premise: s3 data-controls note, linked adjacent to the final claim. Boundary: workload-fit inference; requirements vary by organisation and jurisdiction.

claims.text: OpenAI says session events and saved history expose progress, outcomes and delegated work, while detailed traces remain dashboard-only and usage is best-effort, can change and is not a final bill.
claims.sourceLocator: s8 Overview, Inspect a turn trace, What contributes to cost and Understand token usage; the final trace/export clause carries an adjacent s8 link.

claims.text: The cited independent work supports testing complete outcomes across task horizons and harness choices, but it does not independently verify the Agents API or establish that managed compaction improves a particular workflow.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s9 reports harness sensitivity; s10 reports step-count degradation; s11 defines task-completion horizons and scope limits. Boundary is explicit in the final article.
